name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MCQ_Q67 - Removal of permanent hardness using washing soda

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Permanent hardness of water is removed by treatment with washing soda.

Reason (R): Washing soda reacts with soluble magnesium and calcium sulphate to form insoluble carbonates.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Permanent hardness of water is caused by the presence of soluble calcium and magnesium salts, primarily chlorides and sulphates. Treatment with sodium carbonate (washing soda) effectively softens permanent hard water by converting these soluble divalent metal cations into insoluble carbonate precipitates.

Step 2: Evaluation
Washing soda (\(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3\)) reacts with soluble calcium and magnesium sulphates and chlorides in hard water via double displacement:
\[\mathrm{CaSO}_4 + \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaCO}_3\downarrow + \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\]
\[\mathrm{MgSO}_4 + \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3 \longrightarrow \mathrm{MgCO}_3\downarrow + \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\]
The precipitated insoluble carbonates are readily separated by filtration, thereby eliminating the ions responsible for hardness. Thus, both statements are correct, and the precipitation of insoluble carbonates directly explains why washing soda successfully removes permanent hardness.

Step 3: Conclusion
Both statements are correct and the stated reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

answer.text: Statements A and R both are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A and R both are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_MCQ_Q68 - Transition metals as storage media for hydrogen

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Some metals like platinum and palladium, can be used as storage media for hydrogen.

Reason (R): Platinum and palladium can absorb large volumes of hydrogen.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Certain transition metals, most notably palladium and platinum, possess open interstitial sites in their crystal lattices that allow them to adsorb and absorb substantial quantities of dihydrogen gas, forming interstitial or metallic hydrides.

Step 2: Evaluation
Palladium can accommodate hydrogen gas up to nearly 900 times its own volume through interstitial absorption. Because this occluded hydrogen can be desorbed reversibly upon mild heating or reduction in pressure without altering the structural integrity of the metal, these metals serve as efficient media for hydrogen storage and transportation in the hydrogen economy. Thus, both statements are correct, and the large absorption capacity of these metals provides the direct scientific rationale for their use as hydrogen storage media.

Step 3: Conclusion
Both statements are correct and the stated reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
